advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Thread `body_limit` into `_is_exempt`/`_has_unbreakable_token` instead of using the module-level `BODY_LIMIT` constant.
evidence: 91:     return _has_unbreakable_token(stripped, BODY_LIMIT)
133:         if len(line) > body_limit and not _is_exempt(line, in_fence=in_fence):
`_is_exempt(line: str, *, in_fence: bool)` has no `body_limit` parameter, so it cannot see the caller-supplied limit at all.
The CLI exposes `--body-limit` (line 142), making the two thresholds diverge whenever a non-default value is passed.
advisory.finding: `_is_exempt` calls `_has_unbreakable_token(stripped, BODY_LIMIT)` using the module-level constant instead of the `body_limit` value threaded through `check_message`, so the atomic-token exemption is always computed against 72 even when the caller passes `--body-limit`. A custom body limit is honoured for the overlength check (line 133) but silently ignored when deciding the unbreakable-token carve-out.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a `body_limit` parameter to `_is_exempt` and pass it down to `_has_unbreakable_token`, and pass `body_limit` from the `check_message` loop.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Report the actual file line number (map back through stripped/popped lines) rather than the index into the filtered content list.
evidence: 109:     content = [ln for ln in lines if not ln.strip().startswith("#")]

110:     while content and not content[0].strip():
111:         content.pop(0)
129:     for offset, line in enumerate(content[1:], start=2):
134:             problems.append(f"line {offset} is {len(line)} chars (limit {body_limit}): {line[:56]!r}…")
CONTRIBUTING.md advertises exact line numbers to the user: '  - line 3 is 222 chars (limit 72): ...' (CONTRIBUTING.md:111), reinforcing that the number is meant to be actionable.
advisory.finding: The `line N` numbers in the reported problems are offsets into the filtered `content` list (comment `#` lines removed at line 109 and leading blank lines popped at 110-111), not the actual line numbers in the user's commit-message file. As soon as the message contains any comment line or leading blank before the offending line, the reported number no longer matches what the author sees in their editor.
advisory.suggested_fix: Track original 1-based line numbers when building `content` (e.g. carry `(orig_lineno, text)` tuples) and report the original number.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the trailer detection so common prose lead-ins ('Note:', 'Example:', 'Warning:') are not treated as exempt trailers, or restrict trailer matching to the trailer block / a known key set.
evidence: 42:_TRAILER_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:\s")

89:     if _TRAILER_RE.match(stripped) or _TAG_RE.match(stripped):
90:         return True

The regex requires no space before the colon, but a body line like 'Note: this explanation runs well past seventy-two columns...' starts with the single token 'Note' + ':' + space and therefore matches.
No test exercises a 'Word: ' prose line to distinguish it from a real trailer (tests only cover Signed-off-by/Change-Id/rebar-ticket, test_long_trailer_is_exempt).
advisory.finding: `_TRAILER_RE = ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:\s` matches any prose line that begins with a single word immediately followed by a colon and whitespace (e.g. 'Note: <long sentence>', 'Example: ...', 'Warning: ...'). Such an ordinary wrappable prose line is treated as a trailer and exempted from the 72-column check, a silent false negative.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a body line containing one over-limit atomic token (URL/path) PLUS enough surrounding prose to still exceed the limit is flagged, exercising the `remainder <= limit` guard.
evidence: scripts/check_commit_message_wrap.py:72-73: `remainder = len(line.strip()) - max(len(t) for t in over)` / `return remainder <= limit`
Docstring at scripts/check_commit_message_wrap.py:57-61 states 'one long token followed by lots of prose that should have been moved to the next line ... is [not] exempt'

test_long_url_is_exempt (line 116-122) uses `See https://...x.html` — the line minus the URL is short, so the remainder path is never negative; ABSENCE: no test asserts a URL/path line with substantial trailing prose IS flagged
scripts/check_commit_message_wrap.py:118: `if len(subject) > subject_limit and not _has_unbreakable_token(subject, subject_limit):`
test_overlong_subject_is_flagged (line 106-108) uses only prose 'a subject line that runs well past the fifty character limit'; ABSENCE: no test drives the subject through `_has_unbreakable_token`
advisory.finding: The deliberate `remainder <= limit` guard in `_has_unbreakable_token` (a line that is too long even after removing its single long atomic token must still be flagged) has no test. Every URL/atomic-token exemption test uses a line that is essentially just the token plus a short lead-in, so the branch where `remainder > limit` returns False is never exercised — removing that guard (making any line with one over-limit URL/path exempt) would leave the whole suite green while silently exempting unwrapped prose containing a URL.
merged_from: The subject-line atomic-token exemption path is untested: `check_message` calls `_has_unbreakable_token(subject, subject_limit)` so an over-limit subject that is a single unsplittable token is exempt, but `test_overlong_subject_is_flagged` only uses ordinary prose. A regression in the subject's atomic-token handling (e.g. exempting nothing, or using the wrong limit) would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix:
Add: `assert len(_check(chk, 'feat: t

See https://example.com/x plus a lot of extra prose that pushes this line well over the seventy two column limit here
')) == 1`
